identity.title: Video-Based Optimal Transport for Feedback-Efficient Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Learning complex RL objectives without meticulous reward engineering, while reducing human feedback requirements.

gap.claim: PbRL scalability is limited by high human labeling costs.

contributions.claim: VOTP, a semi-supervised framework that learns reward functions from a handful of labels using Video Foundation Model representations and optimal transport.
An approach for producing high-fidelity pseudo-labels for large unlabeled trajectory datasets by aligning visual trajectories.
Reported evaluation across locomotion, manipulation, visual-distractor, and real-robot settings under limited human feedback.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present VOTP as a video-based optimal-transport approach for semi-supervised, feedback-efficient offline PbRL.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that VOTP outperforms state-of-the-art offline PbRL methods under limited feedback budgets on locomotion and manipulation benchmarks.
The authors report robustness to visual distractors and utility on real robotic tasks, where meaningful rewards are learned with minimal human input.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex RL objectives commonly require meticulous reward engineering.
PbRL can learn rewards from human preferences, but labeling costs hinder scalability.
VOTP combines ViFM visual representations with optimal transport to generate pseudo-labels from few labeled trajectories and much unlabeled data.
The authors report superior performance under limited feedback, robustness to visual distractors, and utility on real robotic tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a feedback-efficiency goal to a concrete mechanism: aligning visual trajectories in pretrained representation space to create pseudo-labels.

lessons.interpretation: A strong method summary can make the intended benefit legible by pairing the bottleneck with the mechanism that addresses it.
lessons.application: When proposing semi-supervised learning, explicitly map the scarce annotation resource to the representation and propagation mechanism used to exploit unlabeled data.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when unlabeled examples are not comparable in a shared representation space or pseudo-label errors are especially costly.

unknowns: The abstract does not quantify the number of labels, feedback budgets, performance gains, or robustness results.
Specific benchmarks, baselines, metrics, distractors, and real-robot task details are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independently verified superiority, correctness, reproducibility, or priority of the claimed novelty.
